rationale: This is the final iteration, so the priority is the design most likely to score well on an unseen track, not further exploration. Iteration 6 is the best result so far (945.42). Every development track finished 20/20, with progress about 0.996 to 0.998 and rms_error about 0.006. Later tweaks did not beat it: kp 5.0 (iteration 8) gave 945.14, kd 1.2 (iteration 9) gave 941.04, mass 0.5 with base_speed 0.95 (iteration 7) gave 941.60, and ki 0.10 (iteration 10) gave 944.10. Those differences are within noise, and each departure from iteration 6 has been neutral or negative, so I resubmit iteration 6 unchanged. Geometry: five line sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m and y = 0.06 m, sensor_size 0.016 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.11 m long by 0.12 m wide, mass 0.6 kg. Controller: base_speed 0.9, kp 4.5, ki 0.05, kd 1.0, sensor_weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], line_loss last_direction. Expected result: the same as iteration 6, about 945 on the development tracks, with 100 percent completion. The main residual losses are line_loss_events (0.1 to 0.5 per run) and completion time (2.0 to 2.6 s). Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error and line_loss_events on each track, plus steering_oscillation and control_effort, to confirm the robustness of this design before the unseen-track race.
